Four things found in two days of one machine's logs: a tunnel that answers and carries badly now says so, and three sources of work done for nothing are gone.

To update, run the new `dpiswitch.exe` from anywhere and accept the offer to install over the installed version (one administrator prompt). Settings, lists, configs and verdicts are kept.

## Tunnels

- **The first tunnel says when it carries badly.** Its state was the answer to one small request: a tunnel losing a quarter of its full-size packets downloaded at 1-2 Mbit/s and said "responding, 61 ms" all evening. The detector times a handshake through the tunnel with every check it makes; when a fifth of the last hour's are three times slower than usual, the header's dot and the overview's state turn yellow -- "responding slowly" -- and the figures stand after the state: the hour's handshake, the usual one, the share of slow ones. Nothing is measured anew and nothing is sent through the tunnel for it. With fewer than 8 checks in the hour there is nothing to say; the second tunnel carries no checks and has no such figure.

## Detector and routes

- **Chrome's own measuring names are not checked.** `beacons*.gvt2.com` and `e2cNN.gcp.gvt2.com` are where Chrome reports its network errors and measures against; the e2c servers answer one time in two on every path, under a new name each time. In two days they took 334 checks of 931 for some 250 connections, and went into the tunnel for an hour and back 13 times. `gvt2.com` and `gvt3.com` are left unchecked and go the default way.
- **A wide network's ranges are waited for, and kept a week.** RIPE computes a network's ranges for as long as it is wide -- 16 s for Amazon's -- and the lookup waited 8: it failed every ten minutes for as long as the network was wanted. The lookup of ranges waits 30 s. A network too wide to lend its way was asked again daily to be thrown away again; it is kept so for a week.

## UDP leak guard

- **The guard is checked out of the adapters that come.** The test packet went out once, when the filters went in -- and after a sleep they are in before Wi-Fi is up: there was nothing to send it from, and the settings said "in place" without "checked" until the core's next start. An adapter that came later, a cable or another network, was never tried at all. The packet now goes out of each set of adapters that lead out, until the engine has it dropped there; where the engine records nothing, three times and no more. The filters themselves were in place all along, ahead of the network.

Core: the fork's 8067c742 (mihomo Alpha 9f053c49).
